text.p: These are significant stories in the Nigerian press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Nigerian ports authority says not to blame for Lagos fuel shortage which state oil firm NNPC says is because ships laden with oil products are not being discharged as a result of disputed debt owed the port group by NNPC.
- Poor visibility resulting from seasonal "harmattan" winds blowing dust from the arid north is causing airlines to divert Lagos-bound flights to Accra, Ghana.
- Aviation experts blame plane crash in Yola northeastern Nigeria last Friday which killed five people on poor visibility.
- A Guardian newspaper survey shows accountancy graduates are in hot demand in otherwise bleak job market in Nigeria.
- Friday and Saturday declared public holidays to mark the Moslem festival of Eid el-Fitr.
- Shell Nigeria unit to spend 2.4 billion naira on community help projects in oil-producing Niger Delta this year, says company chief executive Brian Anderson.
- Nigerian minting company retrenches at least 33 workers.
- Four arrested in midwestern Benin City over fire there last Sunday which burnt a telephone exchange.
- Six former state military administrators may be arraigned before an army panel over alleged questionable activites while in office, sources say.
- Kwara state newspaper in central Nigeria sacks 250 in a move to keep the cash-strapped newspaper afloat.
- Shell Nigeria unit in high gear to develop newly discovered on-shore oil wells.
